sentences.en: Across the world, many countries are experiencing a sleep crisis.
sentences.zh: 放眼全球，许多国家正经历着睡眠危机。

sentences.en: In the United States, 50 to 70 million Americans have sleep disorders.
sentences.zh: 在美国，有5000万到7000万名美国人患有睡眠障碍。

sentences.en: In India, almost 60% of adults get less than six hours of sleep every night.
sentences.zh: 在印度，近60%的成年人每晚睡眠不足六小时。

sentences.en: Sleep deprivation can make us groggy and irritable.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足会让我们昏昏沉沉、烦躁不安。

sentences.en: Chronic sleep deprivation can rewire our brains and wear down our bodies.
sentences.zh: 长期的睡眠不足会重塑我们的大脑，并损耗我们的身体。

sentences.en: It can change how we parent, how we work with others, even what we value.
sentences.zh: 它甚至会改变我们的育儿方式、与他人的协作方式，乃至我们的价值观。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, and in a companion episode on Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》节目，以及《Hidden Brain Plus》的配套剧集，

sentences.en: what happens when a basic human need is jeopardized by an always-on culture,
sentences.zh: 将探讨当一种基本的人类需求受到“全天候”文化威胁时会发生什么，

sentences.en: and techniques to help you get a restful night of sleep.
sentences.zh: 并提供一些帮助你获得安稳睡眠的技巧。

sentences.en: We all know that sleep matters, and we all know what happens when we miss a night of sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道睡眠很重要，也都知道如果一晚没睡会发生什么。

sentences.en: At the University of Washington, sleep researcher Chris Barnes has studied what happens when the
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿大学，睡眠研究员克里斯·巴恩斯研究了当

sentences.en: need for rest and the need to work collide.
sentences.zh: 休息需求与工作需求发生冲突时会发生什么。

sentences.en: He says the consequences of not getting enough sleep extend far beyond what most of us imagine.
sentences.zh: 他说，睡眠不足的后果远比我们大多数人想象的要严重得多。

sentences.en: Chris Barnes, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·巴恩斯，欢迎来到《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm happy to be here, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Chris, you've studied the effects of sleep deprivation for many years.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你研究睡眠不足的影响已经很多年了。

sentences.en: One story in particular has stayed with you.
sentences.zh: 有一个故事让你印象特别深刻。

sentences.en: It involves a man named William Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 它涉及到一个名叫威廉·洛克菲勒的人。

sentences.en: Can you tell me his story?
So William Rockefeller was a train engineer in New York, and he had a route that started early
sentences.zh: 威廉·洛克菲勒是纽约的一名火车司机，他负责的路线是清晨

sentences.en: in the morning from Poughkeepsie headed to New York City.
sentences.zh: 从波基普西出发前往纽约市。

sentences.en: So the reason William Rockefeller ended up in the news one day was because of something that
sentences.zh: 威廉·洛克菲勒之所以有一天会登上新闻，是因为他在

sentences.en: happened as he was making this train journey.
sentences.zh: 执行这次列车任务时发生了一些事情。
告诉我发生了什么，克里斯。

sentences.en: So as he was operating this train early in the morning, he sped through a section of the track
sentences.zh: 当他在清晨驾驶这列火车时，他加速通过了一段限速

sentences.en: in which he could go 70 miles an hour, ended up going a little faster than that, closer to 80 miles
sentences.zh: 为每小时70英里的轨道，结果速度比这还要快，接近每小时80英里，

sentences.en: an hour, and continued that speed as it came to a curve.
sentences.zh: 并且在进入弯道时依然保持着这个速度。

sentences.en: This curve had a speed limit of 35, but he did not slow his train down to that speed fast enough
sentences.zh: 这个弯道的限速是35英里，但他没能足够快地将列车减速到该速度，

sentences.en: I understand that he hit the brake, but just not in time?
sentences.zh: 我明白，他是踩了刹车，但没来得及？

sentences.en: Yes, it was too little too late, and the train derailed.
sentences.zh: 是的，为时已晚，列车脱轨了。

sentences.en: Four people were killed, and 60 were injured.
So when investigators looked into the source of the problem, tell me what they found.
sentences.zh: 那么，当调查人员调查问题根源时，告诉我他们发现了什么。

sentences.en: Well, initially, the train conductor's statement was that he felt like he entered a state of being
sentences.zh: 嗯，起初，火车司机的陈述是他感觉自己在驾驶火车时进入了一种

sentences.en: sort of dazed or mesmerized while he was operating the train.
sentences.zh: 昏昏沉沉或神志恍惚的状态。

sentences.en: Later, it came out that likely he actually fell asleep while he was operating the train,
sentences.zh: 后来，事实证明他很可能是在驾驶火车时真的睡着了，

sentences.en: and then woke up too late to slow the train down to an appropriate speed for that curve.
sentences.zh: 然后醒来得太晚，没能将列车减速到适合该弯道的速度。

sentences.en: So essentially, he fell asleep, and that led him to crash the train.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，他睡着了，这导致他撞毁了火车。

sentences.en: So as the train came roaring up to this curved section of the track,
sentences.zh: 所以当火车呼啸着冲向这段弯道时，

sentences.en: presumably, he woke up and he hit the brakes, but that was too little too late.
sentences.zh: 据推测，他醒了过来并踩了刹车，但已经太晚了。

sentences.en: I understand this train operator also suffered from sleep apnea, Chris?
sentences.zh: 我听说这位火车司机还患有睡眠呼吸暂停症，克里斯？

sentences.en: He had a history of sleep apnea, which is a sleep disorder that is very disruptive to people's sleep.
sentences.zh: 他有睡眠呼吸暂停症病史，这是一种非常干扰人们睡眠的睡眠障碍。

sentences.en: Essentially, when you have sleep apnea, your airway closes off, and you stop breathing.
sentences.zh: 本质上，当你患有睡眠呼吸暂停症时，气道会闭合，导致呼吸停止。

sentences.en: And then, usually, you choke yourself awake, and this might happen as many as hundreds of times per hour.
sentences.zh: 然后，你通常会把自己憋醒，这种情况每小时可能发生多达数百次。

sentences.en: So it is quite disruptive to people's sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以这对人们的睡眠干扰很大。

sentences.en: And even if you think you're getting a lot of sleep while you have sleep apnea,
sentences.zh: 即使你认为自己在患有睡眠呼吸暂停症时睡了很长时间，

sentences.en: the quality of that sleep is poor, and the amount of sleep is usually much less than people think.
sentences.zh: 那种睡眠的质量也很差，而且睡眠总量通常比人们想象的要少得多。

sentences.en: You can imagine how frustrating this would be to experience sleep apnea,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象患有睡眠呼吸暂停症是多么令人沮丧，

sentences.en: where there are so many of these events throughout the night that you don't even remember all of the wakenings,
sentences.zh: 整晚发生这么多起事件，以至于你甚至记不住所有的觉醒时刻，

sentences.en: because they were just too numerous, and you're kind of groggy when they happen.
sentences.zh: 因为次数太多了，而且发生时你还处于昏昏沉沉的状态。

sentences.en: I understand the National Transportation Safety Board investigated this crash that took place, Chris.
sentences.zh: 我了解到美国国家运输安全委员会调查了这起事故，克里斯。

sentences.en: Did they identify a lack of sleep or sleep on the part of the operator as the source of the problem?
sentences.zh: 他们是否将操作员睡眠不足或在工作中睡觉认定为问题的根源？

sentences.en: Well, they mentioned several causal factors,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们提到了几个诱因，

sentences.en: one of which would be his recent change from a day schedule to a morning schedule.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他最近从白班转到了早班。

sentences.en: So there's some potential for circadian disruption,
sentences.zh: 所以存在一些昼夜节律紊乱的可能性，

sentences.en: in addition to his sleep apnea sort of stacking together
sentences.zh: 再加上他的睡眠呼吸暂停症，这些因素叠加在一起，

sentences.en: as setting the stage for a higher likelihood than would otherwise be the case for him falling asleep on the job.
sentences.zh: 为他比平时更容易在工作中睡着创造了条件。

sentences.en: And perhaps it's not surprising that that's exactly what happened to him.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是发生在他身上的事情，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: So this incident took place in December 2013.
And a similar story took place in 2001 in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 2001年在英国也发生过类似的故事。

sentences.en: But this time the problem was not with a train operator, but with a motorist named Gary Hart.
sentences.zh: 但这次的问题不在于火车司机，而在于一位名叫加里·哈特的驾车者。
告诉我那个故事，克里斯。

sentences.en: So Mr. Hart was operating his vehicle,
sentences.zh: 哈特先生当时正在驾驶他的车辆，

sentences.en: which was pulling a trailer that had another car on the trailer.
sentences.zh: 车后拖着一辆拖车，拖车上还载着另一辆车。

sentences.en: And he had driven through much of the night.
sentences.zh: 他几乎开了一整晚的车。

sentences.en: This was an early morning event.
sentences.zh: 这是一起发生在清晨的事件。

sentences.en: And he fell asleep while driving.
And his vehicle veered off the road down an embankment and onto some train tracks.
sentences.zh: 他的车冲出了道路，顺着路堤滑到了铁轨上。

sentences.en: He tried to reverse off the train tracks, but was stuck and could not get his vehicle off.
sentences.zh: 他试图倒车离开铁轨，但被卡住了，无法将车移开。

sentences.en: So he exited the vehicle and called the emergency services.
sentences.zh: 于是他下了车，拨打了紧急服务电话。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, that's when disaster struck.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，灾难就在那时发生了。

sentences.en: So a train was already on those same tracks.
sentences.zh: 当时已经有一列火车行驶在同一条轨道上。

sentences.en: And you can actually hear on his recorded emergency services call,
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以在他录下的紧急服务通话中听到，

sentences.en: the train actually striking his vehicle.
And that train was derailed and deflected in the direction of another train coming the opposite direction,
sentences.zh: 那列火车脱轨并偏向了迎面驶来的另一列火车，

sentences.en: which produced a head-on collision between the two trains.
sentences.zh: 导致两列火车迎头相撞。

sentences.en: That produced several fatalities and many injuries as well.
sentences.zh: 那次事故也造成了多人死亡和受伤。

sentences.en: I understand that 10 people were killed and 82 were injured,
sentences.zh: 我了解到有10人死亡，82人受伤，

sentences.en: making it the worst rail disaster in the United Kingdom in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 使其成为英国21世纪最严重的铁路灾难。

sentences.en: You know, perhaps there were many factors you could argue,
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许你可以争辩说有很多因素，

sentences.en: but one of the principal factors was that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但主要因素之一是，你知道，

sentences.en: Gary Hart drove off the road in the first place because he was asleep.
sentences.zh: 加里·哈特最初冲出道路是因为他睡着了。

sentences.en: Fell asleep at the wheel and woke up as his vehicle was going down that embankment
sentences.zh: 在方向盘前睡着了，醒来时车子正顺着路堤滑向

sentences.en: But that was obviously too late to prevent the disaster from occurring.
sentences.zh: 但这显然已经太晚了，无法阻止灾难的发生。

sentences.en: So typically when incidents like this take place, Chris,
sentences.zh: 所以通常当这类事件发生时，克里斯，

sentences.en: our tendency is to blame the people involved,
sentences.zh: 我们的倾向是责怪相关人员，

sentences.en: to blame the motorist who fell asleep,
to blame the train operator who was drowsy.
sentences.zh: 责怪昏昏欲睡的火车司机。

sentences.en: these individuals have to take responsibility for what happened.
sentences.zh: 这些人必须为发生的事情承担责任。

sentences.en: But you say that this ignores a more serious part of the problem, Chris?
sentences.zh: 但你说这忽略了问题中更严重的一部分，克里斯？

sentences.en: So we usually prefer simple, easy answers.
sentences.zh: 我们通常更喜欢简单、容易的答案。

sentences.en: We prefer to look for proximal factors that are simple to diagnose,
sentences.zh: 我们更倾向于寻找容易诊断的近因，

sentences.en: and then we can dismiss the whole thing, like operator error.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以把一切归咎于“操作失误”之类的原因，从而不再深究。

sentences.en: Human error is sort of a catch-all that we often use
sentences.zh: “人为失误”是我们经常使用的一种万能借口，

sentences.en: when we have disasters like these happen.
But we don't often ask the question,
sentences.zh: 但我们很少问这样一个问题：

sentences.en: okay, why did that human error occur?
sentences.zh: 好吧，为什么会发生这种人为失误？

sentences.en: Why did this person fall asleep while they were doing something
sentences.zh: 为什么这个人会在做一些

sentences.en: that is dangerous to do while they're asleep?
sentences.zh: 在睡着时做会很危险的事情时睡着了？

sentences.en: So we need to zoom out and look at more systemic factors surrounding that decision
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要拉远视角，审视围绕该决策的更多系统性因素，

sentences.en: without necessarily totally absolving the person who fell asleep on the job.
sentences.zh: 而不必完全免除那个在工作中睡着的人的责任。

sentences.en: They bear some responsibility as well.
sentences.zh: 他们也承担一定的责任。
但这从来都不是那么简单。

sentences.en: This is always something that occurs in the context of many other factors,
sentences.zh: 这总是在许多其他因素的背景下发生的，

sentences.en: often which operate in concert in the same direction,
sentences.zh: 这些因素往往同时起作用，朝着同一个方向，
推动人们走向睡眠不足。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's not like William Rockefeller and Gary Hart
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，并不是说威廉·洛克菲勒和加里·哈特

sentences.en: had these long histories of accidents and probleMs.
sentences.zh: 有着长期的事故和问题记录。

sentences.en: These were one-off incidents, obviously terrible incidents,
sentences.zh: 这些都是一次性的事件，显然是可怕的事件，

sentences.en: but they were one-off incidents, which does raise the question,
sentences.zh: 但它们是一次性的，这就提出了一个问题：

sentences.en: what else was going on besides what was happening in these individual people's lives?
sentences.zh: 除了这些个人生活中的事情之外，还发生了什么？

sentences.en: On other days of driving, they were perfectly safe.
sentences.zh: 在其他驾驶的日子里，他们是非常安全的。

sentences.en: They did not fall asleep at the wheel.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有在方向盘前睡着。

sentences.en: And there were other people that day who didn't fall asleep,
sentences.zh: 那天也有其他人没有睡着，

sentences.en: but those other people, perhaps in the right context, might make the same mistake.
sentences.zh: 但那些人，在适当的环境下，也可能会犯同样的错误。

sentences.en: So, Chris, you became a father to twins in 2019.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯，你在2019年成为了双胞胎的父亲。

sentences.en: You already had a three-year-old at home at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时你家里已经有一个三岁的孩子了。

sentences.en: I'm imagining this was a time in your life when you weren't getting much sleep?
sentences.zh: 我想象那段时间你一定没怎么睡过觉？
是的，那真是让人难以承受。

sentences.en: The way I like to think of it is imagine all of the challenges and difficulties of a newborn
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样想：想象一下新生儿带来的所有挑战和困难，

sentences.en: and how disruptive that is to your sleep, and then add a second newborn to that same equation.
sentences.zh: 以及这对你的睡眠有多大的干扰，然后再加上第二个新生儿。

sentences.en: So, if somebody hands you a second baby and says, here, deal with this as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人递给你第二个婴儿说，来，你也处理一下这个。

sentences.en: So, all of the feeding and changing cycles are longer, and nobody sleeps well in the situation.
sentences.zh: 所有的喂养和换尿布周期都变长了，在这种情况下没人能睡好。

sentences.en: I certainly didn't sleep very well.
And you also had another little one at home at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且你当时家里还有一个小家伙。

sentences.en: Yes, I had a three-year-old who also required attention and love and caring for the cumulative duties at home
sentences.zh: 是的，我有一个三岁的孩子，也需要关注、爱和照顾，家里累积的责任

sentences.en: between the twins and my three-year-old were quite high.
sentences.zh: 在双胞胎和三岁孩子之间是非常繁重的。

sentences.en: So, I actually have very little memory of that time period other than sluggishly washing bottles
sentences.zh: 所以，我对那段时间几乎没有什么记忆，除了昏昏沉沉地洗奶瓶、

sentences.en: and changing diapers and just trying to survive.
sentences.zh: 换尿布，只是努力生存下去。

sentences.en: So, one night you get an urgent call from your mom.
sentences.zh: 那么，一天晚上你接到了母亲的紧急电话。

sentences.en: Describe for me what she said and what happened next, Chris.
sentences.zh: 描述一下她说了什么，接下来发生了什么，克里斯。

sentences.en: So, for context, my parents, especially my father, had been in poor health for a few decades.
sentences.zh: 背景是，我的父母，尤其是我的父亲，健康状况已经不佳几十年了。

sentences.en: And so, some corner of my mind was always concerned that the next call I get from my mom
sentences.zh: 所以，我内心深处总会担心，我从母亲那里接到的下一个电话，

sentences.en: could be that call that perhaps my father was dying.
sentences.zh: 可能就是我父亲去世的消息。

sentences.en: So, in this particular occasion, my mother called me at three in the morning.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这次特定的情况下，我母亲在凌晨三点给我打了电话。

sentences.en: And that timing is already indicative that something is not going well.
sentences.zh: 那个时间点本身就已经预示着情况不妙。

sentences.en: So, she called me quite distressed, saying that she had found my father lying on the floor,
sentences.zh: 她当时非常心烦意乱地给我打电话，说她发现我父亲躺在地板上，

sentences.en: It wasn't clear how long he had been there, but they were on their way to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 不清楚他躺了多久，但他们已经在去医院的路上了。

sentences.en: And so, my first thought was, okay, this is the call I've been expecting.
sentences.zh: 所以我第一个念头是，好吧，这通电话我早有预料。

sentences.en: I need to go see them right away.
Like, this might be my last chance to see my father while he's still alive.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我见父亲最后一面的机会了，趁他还活着。

sentences.en: So, I'm imagining that you probably hopped in the car and raced to the hospital, Chris.
sentences.zh: 我想你当时肯定跳上车，飞奔去了医院，克里斯。

sentences.en: So, the hospital was about an hour from my home.
sentences.zh: 医院离我家大约一个小时的路程。

sentences.en: And so, I immediately got into the car and drove down there, despite it being roughly three in the morning,
sentences.zh: 所以我立刻上了车，开车赶了过去，尽管当时大概是凌晨三点，

sentences.en: in a time period in which I was already not sleeping much anyway.
sentences.zh: 而且那段时间我本来就没怎么睡好。

sentences.en: So, tell me what happened once you got to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我你到医院后发生了什么。

sentences.en: I got to the hospital and spent a few hours talking with my parents.
sentences.zh: 我到了医院，和父母聊了几个小时。

sentences.en: My dad, turns out, he was okay.
It was just a scary event that wasn't so dangerous to his health after all.
sentences.zh: 那只是一场虚惊，对他的健康并没有什么大碍。

sentences.en: I had that chance to spend some time with him.
sentences.zh: 我有机会陪了他一会儿。

sentences.en: But I still had two babies at home and a three-year-old.
sentences.zh: 但我家里还有两个婴儿和一个三岁的孩子。

sentences.en: And my wife at the time was the only one looking after all three of them.
sentences.zh: 当时我妻子一个人照顾他们三个。

sentences.en: So, I'm imagining you must have jumped back in the car and now try to race home.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜你一定又跳上车，赶着回家了。

sentences.en: So, I felt both physically and emotionally exhausted.
The physical exhaustion was due to an accumulation of sleep deprivation over the preceding weeks and more.
sentences.zh: 身体上的疲惫是因为过去几周甚至更长时间里睡眠不足的累积。

sentences.en: And plus the wakening and the rapid drive down to the hospital at 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 再加上凌晨三点被惊醒，又匆忙开车去医院。

sentences.en: Plus the emotional exhaustion of thinking that perhaps this is when my father's about to die.
sentences.zh: 还有心理上的疲惫，因为我以为父亲可能快不行了。

sentences.en: So, those two stacked on top of each other just left me feeling completely drained.
sentences.zh: 这两者叠加在一起，让我感到彻底被掏空了。

sentences.en: I did not crash on the way home.
sentences.zh: 回家的路上我没有出车祸。

sentences.en: But I did have a moment where I fell asleep while driving on the freeway for probably a few seconds.
sentences.zh: 但我确实有那么一瞬间，在高速公路上开车时睡着了，大概几秒钟。

sentences.en: I can only guess, but my estimation, it was somewhere around three to five seconds going straight on I-5 at highway speeds.
sentences.zh: 我只能猜测，估计是在5号州际公路上以高速行驶时，睡了三到五秒。

sentences.en: Now, three to five seconds going at 60, 70 miles an hour, you cover a lot of distance in three to five seconds, Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，以每小时60到70英里的速度行驶，三到五秒钟能跑很长一段距离。

sentences.en: And as soon as I woke up, I had this jolt of fear and guilt and anger at myself knowing that I had just done a really stupid thing.
sentences.zh: 我一醒来，就感到一阵恐惧、内疚和对自己愤怒，因为我知道自己做了一件非常愚蠢的事。

sentences.en: That there is no way I should have made that decision, that I just put not only my life at risk, but all the drivers around me.
sentences.zh: 我绝不该做出那个决定，我不仅让自己陷入危险，还危及了周围所有的司机。

sentences.en: Sometimes I still think about that moment.
sentences.zh: 有时我还会想起那一刻。

sentences.en: And I think about the fact that in the multiverse, some swath of that multiverse, I am the villain in some family story.
sentences.zh: 我想到在多元宇宙中，在某个分支里，我成了某个家庭故事里的反派。

sentences.en: Because as I fell asleep, I crashed into another vehicle and caused some tragedies.
sentences.zh: 因为我睡着了，撞上了另一辆车，酿成了悲剧。

sentences.en: So, we've been talking about individual stories here.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在谈论个人的故事。

sentences.en: And people can say, well, these are anecdotes.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会说，这些只是轶事。

sentences.en: One comes from places like Taiwan and Singapore, where traffic crashes often seem to follow a pattern.
sentences.zh: 其中一些来自台湾和新加坡等地，那里的交通事故似乎往往遵循某种模式。

sentences.en: What do we see in these places, Chris?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们在这些地方看到了什么？

sentences.en: Yes, this is quite an interesting pattern that my co-authors and I found.
sentences.zh: 是的，我和我的合著者发现了一个非常有趣的模式。

sentences.en: When my co-author, Sam Yam, he's a professor at National University of Singapore, who was interested in the idea of soccer being a global phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我的合著者山姆·亚姆（Sam Yam）是新加坡国立大学的教授，他一直对足球作为一种全球现象很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so, what we hypothesized and what we found empirically was that there is a spike in car crashes, both in Singapore and Taiwan,
sentences.zh: 我们假设并从经验中发现，在新加坡和台湾，

sentences.en: following major soccer games that are played in Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲重大足球比赛后，车祸数量会出现激增。

sentences.en: And presumably, that's because the games in Europe are played at a time when it's presumably early morning in Asia?
sentences.zh: 大概是因为欧洲的比赛时间，在亚洲正好是清晨？

sentences.en: So, the soccer games in Europe are played at reasonable times for people to watch in Europe, which are generally unreasonable times for people to watch in Asia.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的足球比赛时间对欧洲观众来说很合理，但对亚洲观众来说通常很不合理。

sentences.en: And soccer is probably not as popular per capita in Asia as it is in Europe, but there are a lot of people in Asia, and many of them are soccer fans.
sentences.zh: 虽然足球在亚洲的人均普及率可能不如欧洲，但亚洲人口众多，其中有很多足球迷。

sentences.en: And from some of our preliminary surveys that we did,
sentences.zh: 根据我们做的一些初步调查，

sentences.en: we found that a surprising number of people in Asia are staying up very late into the night or very early in the morning to watch these games live.
sentences.zh: 我们发现亚洲有相当多的人熬夜到很晚，或者起得很早，为了看这些比赛的直播。

sentences.en: And this is, unfortunately, considerably cutting into the sleep that they get that night.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这严重压缩了他们当晚的睡眠时间。

sentences.en: It appears that as a result of that missed sleep, their risk of a car crash goes up.
sentences.zh: 看来由于睡眠不足，他们发生车祸的风险增加了。

sentences.en: And so, that's exactly what we observe in the data.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们在数据中观察到的情况。

sentences.en: You studied taxi crashes with a large taxi company in Singapore and also another data set which tracked really all auto crashes in Taiwan over a period of a few years.
sentences.zh: 你研究了新加坡一家大型出租车公司的事故，以及另一个追踪了台湾几年内所有汽车事故的数据集。

sentences.en: So, we found the same general pattern in these two very different locations in Asia.
sentences.zh: 我们在亚洲这两个截然不同的地方发现了同样的普遍模式。

sentences.en: And there's an interesting nuance on top of that as well, that the effect scales with the popularity of the soccer teams that are playing in Europe.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个有趣的细微差别，这种影响的程度与欧洲参赛球队的受欢迎程度成正比。

sentences.en: So, if those teams are more popular, then we see a larger spike in car crashes the next day in both Singapore and Taiwan.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果那些球队更受欢迎，我们在新加坡和台湾第二天看到的车祸激增就越明显。

sentences.en: When we hear tragic stories of people making grave mistakes as a consequence of sleep deprivation, it's tempting to believe that would never happen to us.
sentences.zh: 当我们听到人们因睡眠不足而犯下严重错误导致悲剧的故事时，很容易认为这种事绝不会发生在自己身上。

sentences.en: That could never happen to us.
sentences.zh: 那绝不可能发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: But the tragic stories we hear are only extreme examples of a universal truth.
sentences.zh: 但我们听到的悲剧故事只是一个普遍真理的极端例子。

sentences.en: Sleep deprivation can profoundly change our judgment and our behavior.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足会深刻地改变我们的判断力和行为。

sentences.en: When we come back, the complex consequences of not getting enough sleep and what you can do about it.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨睡眠不足的复杂后果以及你可以采取的应对措施。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。
我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: How often do you lag through the day, tired and foggy, dreaming of the minute you'll hop into bed for some sleep?
sentences.zh: 你有多频繁地在白天感到疲惫不堪、昏昏沉沉，梦想着能立刻躺下睡上一觉？

sentences.en: You tell yourself that you'll change things in your lifestyle to get more sleep on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 你告诉自己要改变生活方式，保证规律的睡眠。

sentences.en: But that day never comes, and you find yourself stuck in cycles of chronic sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 但那一天永远不会到来，你发现自己陷入了慢性睡眠不足的循环中。

sentences.en: At the University of Washington, Chris Barnes says that while most of us know the consequences of poor sleep, we underestimate how profoundly it can affect us.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学的克里斯·巴恩斯（Chris Barnes）表示，虽然我们大多数人都知道睡眠不足的后果，但我们低估了它对我们影响的深度。

sentences.en: Chris, we've all heard about how a lack of sleep can affect our physical health and even our mental health, but you say there are more insidious effects.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们都听说过睡眠不足会影响身体健康甚至心理健康，但你说还有更隐蔽的影响。

sentences.en: One unfolded in 2018 when World Cup soccer fans were gathered in Moscow, and it involves a driver named Chinggis Anarbek Ulu.
sentences.zh: 2018年世界杯足球赛在莫斯科举行时，就发生了一起涉及司机钦吉斯·阿纳尔别克·乌鲁（Chinggis Anarbek Ulu）的事件。
zh_words: 钦吉斯·阿纳尔别克·乌鲁

sentences.en: Paint me a picture of what happened that day, Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，请描述一下那天发生了什么。

sentences.en: So Ulu was a taxi driver driving in a pretty crowded environment because of the soccer game that was going on, and he suddenly veered onto a sidewalk and accelerated,
sentences.zh: 乌鲁是一名出租车司机，由于当时正在进行足球比赛，环境非常拥挤，他突然转向人行道并加速，

sentences.en: running his car into a crowd of people there.
Immediately after plowing into the crowd of people, he exited his vehicle and fled the scene.
sentences.zh: 在冲入人群后，他立即下车逃离了现场。

sentences.en: Do we know what happened that day and how the accident came about and why he ran away, Chris?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们知道那天发生了什么，事故是怎么发生的，以及他为什么要逃跑吗？

sentences.en: An investigation and interview of Ulu indicates that he had been working for approximately 20 hours straight on shift, and he was clearly quite tired while he was driving.
sentences.zh: 对乌鲁的调查和访谈显示，他已经连续工作了大约20个小时，开车时显然非常疲劳。

sentences.en: And according to his perspective, he was drifting off and was looking to allow a pedestrian to pass by, and then he says that he hit the accelerator instead of the brake.
sentences.zh: 据他自己说，他当时昏昏欲睡，本想让行人先过，结果他说他把油门当成了刹车。

sentences.en: So he had intended to stop and had unfortunately done the opposite.
sentences.zh: 所以他本想停车，却不幸做了相反的操作。

sentences.en: So what strikes me about the story, Chris, isn't that he just fell asleep at the wheel and ended up hurting lots of people,
sentences.zh: 克里斯，这个故事让我震惊的不是他开车时睡着了导致多人受伤，

sentences.en: but that he made the split-second decision to flee the scene afterwards.
sentences.zh: 而是他事后做出了逃离现场的瞬间决定。

sentences.en: In some ways, the story speaks to some of your research because you've studied how a poor night's sleep can damage our ability to make good decisions, can damage our judgment.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这个故事印证了你的一些研究，因为你研究过睡眠不足如何损害我们做出正确决策的能力，损害我们的判断力。

sentences.en: There's a large body of research to indicate that sleep deprivation undermines our decision-making in general, and I do have some research in this area.
sentences.zh: 有大量研究表明，睡眠不足会削弱我们的整体决策能力，我确实在这个领域做过一些研究。

sentences.en: The general theme across this research is that we are much worse decision-makers when we are sleep-deprived.
sentences.zh: 这些研究的共同主题是，我们在睡眠不足时，决策能力会差得多。

sentences.en: This is especially the case for any decisions that we make that are non-routine, that are novel,
sentences.zh: 对于任何非例行、新颖的决策，尤其如此，

sentences.en: and you have to figure things out on the spot rather than simply enacting a previous decision.
sentences.zh: 你必须当场解决问题，而不是简单地执行之前的决定。

sentences.en: So I could imagine that an unexpected incident like a car crash or running into people would be a very novel situation in which you have to rapidly make a decision,
sentences.zh: 所以我可以想象，像车祸或撞人这样的突发事件，是一个非常新颖的情况，你必须迅速做出决定，

sentences.en: and you are impaired in that decision process.
sentences.zh: 而你的决策过程受到了损害。

sentences.en: So it's perhaps not surprising that people make poor decisions in these contexts.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在这种情况下做出糟糕的决定，或许并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So you've looked not just at how the quality of our work might suffer as a result of sleep deprivation,
sentences.zh: 你不仅研究了睡眠不足如何影响工作质量，

sentences.en: but also you've looked into the relationship between a lack of sleep and unethical conduct?
sentences.zh: 还研究了睡眠不足与不道德行为之间的关系？

sentences.en: This was some of my favorite research that I've ever engaged with, and the idea here is that people in the context of work are faced with many temptations.
sentences.zh: 这是我做过的最喜欢的课题之一，其核心理念是，人们在工作中面临许多诱惑。

sentences.en: So you might have a temptation to cut some corners, maybe tell a small lie, maybe take credit for someone else's work, maybe blame somebody else for your mistakes.
sentences.zh: 你可能会有走捷径的诱惑，也许撒个小谎，也许窃取别人的工作成果，也许把自己的错误归咎于他人。

sentences.en: Whatever form of work you have, there's probably some form of unethical behavior that you could engage in that might have some personal benefit.
sentences.zh: 无论你从事什么工作，都可能存在某种不道德行为，能带来个人利益。

sentences.en: Fortunately, most of the time, most of us are able to resist those temptations, and that's great.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，大多数时候，我们大多数人都能抵御这些诱惑，这很好。

sentences.en: But there's clear evidence to indicate that when people are sleep deprived, their ability to exert self-control,
sentences.zh: 但有明确证据表明，当人们睡眠不足时，他们行使自控力的能力，

sentences.en: their ability to resist impulsiveness and cave to those temptations is eroded.
sentences.zh: 他们抵御冲动并屈服于诱惑的能力会受到侵蚀。

sentences.en: So we see that when people are sleep deprived, their likelihood of behaving unethically tends to go up.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到，当人们睡眠不足时，他们做出不道德行为的可能性往往会增加。

sentences.en: And what I find especially fascinating about this is that you can see the same person behaving more unethically or less unethically on different days based in part on how much and how well they slept the night before.
sentences.zh: 我特别着迷的一点是，你可以看到同一个人在不同日子里，因为前一晚睡眠质量和时长的不同，表现得更不道德或更道德。

sentences.en: And when you say sleep deprivation, Chris, are we talking about an hour less of sleep, five hours less of sleep?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，当你提到睡眠不足时，是指少睡一小时，还是少睡五小时？

sentences.en: I think of this as a relatively continuous scale where you will get the worst results if you get zero hours of sleep, but even small amounts of lost sleep matter.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个相对连续的量表，如果你一小时都不睡，结果会最差，但即使是少睡一点点也有影响。

sentences.en: There are some pretty compelling studies, some of my research, but also a much larger body of research,
sentences.zh: 有一些非常有说服力的研究，包括我的一些研究，以及更大规模的研究，

sentences.en: that finds that even an hour of lost sleep can have meaningful effects on outcomes that we care about, like workplace injuries or work engagement or moral awareness.
sentences.zh: 发现即使少睡一小时，也会对我们关心的结果产生重大影响，比如工伤、工作投入度或道德意识。

sentences.en: There are even some nap studies that allow people an opportunity to have like a 10 or a 15 minute nap.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一些午睡研究，允许人们小睡10到15分钟。

sentences.en: And that amount of sleep is enough to move the needle on some important outcomes like performance.
sentences.zh: 这种睡眠量足以改变一些重要结果，比如工作表现。

sentences.en: Some of my research indicates that when people are sleep deprived, their moral awareness is lower.
sentences.zh: 我的一些研究表明，当人们睡眠不足时，他们的道德意识会降低。

sentences.en: So they're less likely to even appreciate that there's a moral aspect to the decision that they're making.
sentences.zh: 所以他们甚至不太可能意识到自己所做的决定具有道德层面。

sentences.en: They just treat it as a non-moral type of decision rather than seeing the layers of nuance that are often entailed in a moral decision.
sentences.zh: 他们只是将其视为一种非道德的决定，而不是看到道德决策中通常包含的细微差别。

sentences.en: So that their sleep deprivation sort of simplifies their decision process in a way that fails to engage their moral frameworks.
sentences.zh: 所以睡眠不足简化了他们的决策过程，导致他们无法运用道德框架。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another overlooked consequence of sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈睡眠不足的另一个被忽视的后果。

sentences.en: In 2014, the ESPN sportscaster Courtney Cronin came under fire for a live television appearance.
sentences.zh: 2014年，ESPN体育主播考特尼·克罗宁（Courtney Cronin）因一次电视直播表现而受到抨击。
克里斯，告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: So she had called in to a live ESPN radio show.
sentences.zh: 她当时连线参加了一个ESPN的直播广播节目。

sentences.en: And she was covering the NFL Combine in Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 当时她正在印第安纳波利斯报道NFL选秀训练营（NFL Combine）。

sentences.en: She joins us on the Home of the Bears ESPN 1000 on the hotline.
sentences.zh: 她在热线电话上加入了我们“熊队之家”ESPN 1000的节目。

sentences.en: And she was having some technical difficulties with her earbuds.
sentences.zh: 当时她的耳机出现了一些技术故障。

sentences.en: And you can actually see in the recording that she was getting some very annoying feedback.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以在录像中看到，她听到了一些非常烦人的反馈音。

sentences.en: And you can see the frustration mount on her face.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到她脸上的挫败感在增加。

sentences.en: And then at some point, she rips out her earbuds and says an expletive live on the air.
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时刻，她扯下耳机，在直播中说了一句脏话。

sentences.en: And everything else kind of unfolded.
So Courtney Cronin blamed this outburst on sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 所以考特尼·克罗宁把这次爆发归咎于睡眠不足。

sentences.en: But at a larger level, Chris, can you talk about how a lack of sleep can make us turn molehills into mountains?
sentences.zh: 但从更宏观的角度来看，克里斯，你能谈谈睡眠不足如何让我们把小事化大吗？

sentences.en: Sleep deprivation has some pretty powerful effects on moods and mood regulation.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足对情绪和情绪调节有相当强大的影响。

sentences.en: So we see that when people are sleep deprived, they tend to have higher levels of irritation and frustration and anger, sometimes higher levels of depression.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们睡眠不足时，往往会有更高水平的烦躁、挫败感和愤怒，有时甚至会有更高水平的抑郁。

sentences.en: And then emotional control becomes more difficult.
sentences.zh: 情绪控制变得更加困难。

sentences.en: And this is due in part to the way different parts of our brain work together.
sentences.zh: 这部分归因于我们大脑不同部分协同工作的方式。

sentences.en: The prefrontal cortex and the amygdala and the way that they interact with each other.
sentences.zh: 前额叶皮层和杏仁核，以及它们之间相互作用的方式。
那种自我调节的效果变差了。

sentences.en: So people's emotions tend to be a lot more lumpy and wavy and big.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的情绪往往波动更大、更剧烈。

sentences.en: And exactly as you say, when we're sleep deprived, something that would normally be more of a molehill looks like more of a mountain.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，当我们睡眠不足时，本来只是一件小事，看起来却像是一座大山。

sentences.en: And so we get big emotional reactions when people are sleep deprived.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们睡眠不足时，会产生强烈的情绪反应。

sentences.en: There's even some evidence that sleep deprivation may be connected to major disasters.
sentences.zh: 甚至有证据表明，睡眠不足可能与重大灾难有关。

sentences.en: On March 23rd, 2005, the Texas-based oil company BP suffered one of the worst industrial disasters in history.
sentences.zh: 2005年3月23日，总部位于德克萨斯州的石油公司英国石油公司（BP）遭遇了历史上最严重的工业灾难之一。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened and how sleep might be implicated in what happened, Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，告诉我发生了什么，以及睡眠如何与所发生的事情有关。

sentences.en: So they had overfilled one of their fuel towers.
sentences.zh: 他们加满了其中一个燃料塔。

sentences.en: And one of the automated systems then vented some of this fuel, which was then ignited.
sentences.zh: 其中一个自动化系统随后排放了一些燃料，接着被点燃了。

sentences.en: It was causing an explosion, raining down this flaming fuel on the trailers of the employees down below, causing several fatalities and injuries as well.
sentences.zh: 这引发了爆炸，燃烧的燃料雨点般落在下方员工的拖车上，造成了多人死亡和受伤。

sentences.en: So when they later investigated what happened, one of the potential causal factors was about a month straight of 12-hour shifts for the employees who were involved.
sentences.zh: 后来调查事故原因时，其中一个潜在的诱因是相关员工连续一个月都在上12小时的轮班。

sentences.en: So this was a tremendous accumulation of sleep debt from missed sleep over this time period.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在这段时间内因睡眠不足而积累的巨大睡眠债。

sentences.en: It wasn't just the 12-hour days, but also the long commute.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是每天12小时的工作，还有漫长的通勤时间。

sentences.en: Some of these employees had two-hour commutes on top of these 12-hour days.
sentences.zh: 有些员工在每天12小时的工作之外，还要忍受两小时的通勤。

sentences.en: So there was a lot of missed sleep in the period leading up to the incident.
sentences.zh: 所以在事故发生前的那段时间里，他们严重睡眠不足。

sentences.en: I mean, there were eventually 15 workers killed and 180 people injured.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最终有15名工人死亡，180人受伤。

sentences.en: And according to the investigation, one of the people involved had had an accumulated sleep debt of 43 hours.
sentences.zh: 根据调查，其中一名相关人员累计睡眠债达到了43小时。

sentences.en: So this is why I'm a little skeptical when people say missing an hour or two or three is not a big deal, because it's not just that one or two or three hours.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当人们说少睡一两个小时没什么大不了时，我会持怀疑态度，因为这不仅仅是那一两个小时的问题。

sentences.en: It's the accumulation of many such nights of sleep debt.
sentences.zh: 这是许多个夜晚睡眠债累积的结果。

sentences.en: There was even a recent report that looked at the relationship between nuclear disaster and sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 最近甚至有一份报告研究了核灾难与睡眠剥夺之间的关系。

sentences.en: So it is perhaps not surprising that several of these events tend to occur very early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 所以，其中几起事件往往发生在清晨，这或许并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So both Chernobyl and Three Mile Island, these events happened between 1.30 in the morning and 4 o'clock in the morning is sort of the most important timing of these events.
sentences.zh: 切尔诺贝利和三哩岛事件都发生在凌晨1点半到4点之间，这是这些事件发生的最关键时间段。

sentences.en: And these are times at which people tend to be at a poor state of mind from their circadian rhythms, pushing them towards sleep.
sentences.zh: 在这些时间里，人们由于昼夜节律的影响，往往处于精神状态不佳的阶段，身体会促使他们进入睡眠。

sentences.en: And when they are working these shifts, it means that they have a work shift that is misaligned with their own natural circadian rhythm, which tends to leave them sleep deprived.
sentences.zh: 当他们轮班工作时，意味着他们的工作时间与自身的自然昼夜节律不一致，这往往会导致他们睡眠不足。

sentences.en: And these are very complicated systems that they're working with, which is especially a problem when there's something novel that occurs.
sentences.zh: 他们操作的是非常复杂的系统，当出现新情况时，问题尤为严重。

sentences.en: So something goes wrong that doesn't typically go wrong.
sentences.zh: 也就是发生了通常不会发生的故障。

sentences.en: And now you have to figure out on the fly how to deal with this in a state in which you are impaired from sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 现在你必须在睡眠剥夺导致的状态下，临时想办法应对。

sentences.en: So of all the times at which these disasters tend to occur, that is the most dangerous time.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这些灾难容易发生的所有时间点中，那是极其危险的时刻。

sentences.en: That's when we see that it has happened, at least in those particular events.
sentences.zh: 至少在那些特定的事件中，我们看到灾难就是在那时发生的。

sentences.en: You know, many of us are sleep deprived, but we're not in charge of a nuclear plant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们很多人都睡眠不足，但我们并不负责核电站。

sentences.en: But of course, some people are in charge of a nuclear plant and they have circadian rhythms too.
sentences.zh: 但当然，有些人负责核电站，他们也有昼夜节律。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, these nuclear plants have to be operated 24 hours a day,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这些核电站必须24小时运转，

sentences.en: which means some of these employees have to work at circadian unfriendly times where their biological drive is to sleep.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一些员工必须在不符合昼夜节律的时间工作，而此时他们的生物钟驱动他们去睡觉。

sentences.en: And instead, we have them wake and operate complicated machinery.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们让他们保持清醒并操作复杂的机器。

sentences.en: And then they go home and their schedule says they should be sleeping, but their biological drive is to be awake and do waking activities.
sentences.zh: 然后他们回家，日程表上写着他们应该睡觉，但他们的生物钟却驱动他们保持清醒并进行活动。

sentences.en: So when we have such circadian misalignment, not only are we less alert and less effective when we are trying to do waking activity,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们出现这种昼夜节律失调时，不仅在试图进行清醒活动时警觉性降低、效率变差，

sentences.en: but our sleep then becomes much more challenging as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的睡眠也会变得更加困难。

sentences.en: I want to talk about one other common source of sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈另一个常见的睡眠剥夺来源。

sentences.en: On March 11, 2018, a sightseeing helicopter crashed into the East River off the Upper East Side of Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 2018年3月11日，一架观光直升机坠毁在曼哈顿上东区附近的东河中。

sentences.en: Five people ended up being killed.
Tell me what happened and how sleep might be connected to the incident, Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，告诉我发生了什么，以及睡眠可能与这次事故有何关联。

sentences.en: So this was a pilot and five passengers taking a tour in New York City.
sentences.zh: 当时是一名飞行员和五名乘客在纽约市进行观光飞行。

sentences.en: So they were flying near the Upper East Side.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在上东区附近飞行。

sentences.en: And there were witnesses that said this helicopter started going down fast as if it were going to land on firm ground.
sentences.zh: 有目击者称，这架直升机开始快速下降，看起来像是要降落在坚实的地面上。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, it did land in the water and then capsized, turned over sideways.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，它降落在了水里，然后倾覆，侧翻了过来。

sentences.en: And the pilot was able to escape.
But the passengers, they had multiple layers of harnesses and they were unable to escape.
sentences.zh: 但乘客们身上有多层安全带，他们无法逃脱。

sentences.en: When investigators try to find out what caused the crash, Chris, what did they find?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，当调查人员试图找出坠机原因时，他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: One of the passengers was turned sideways with his legs outside of the helicopter, which put his supplemental harness sort of dangling towards some of the flight controls.
sentences.zh: 其中一名乘客侧身，双腿伸在直升机外，这使得他的辅助安全带悬挂在一些飞行控制装置附近。

sentences.en: And so he leaned back and then suddenly leaned forward.
sentences.zh: 他向后靠，然后突然向前倾。

sentences.en: And this pulled his supplemental harness against the fuel release control.
sentences.zh: 这拉动了他的辅助安全带，触碰到了燃油释放控制装置。

sentences.en: That's what depowered the helicopter such that it started its rapid descent.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致直升机失去动力并开始快速下降的原因。

sentences.en: So clearly, this accident had a direct cause, but there was also potentially an indirect cause.
sentences.zh: 显然，这次事故有直接原因，但可能也存在间接原因。

sentences.en: The date of the crash was March 11, 2018, as I said.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，坠机日期是2018年3月11日。

sentences.en: But it was also the start of daylight saving time in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但那也是美国夏令时的开始。

sentences.en: On that Sunday, the clocks in many parts of the country jumped forward by an hour overnight, meaning that people got one hour less of sleep.
sentences.zh: 那个星期天，全国许多地方的钟表在夜间拨快了一小时，意味着人们少睡了一个小时。
所以你的手表显示是早上6点，

sentences.en: on your watch, but your body clock feels like it's still 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 但你的生物钟感觉还是早上5点。

sentences.en: What do we know, Chris, about the relationship between that last hour of sleep on daylight saving time weekend and accidents and crashes from nationwide data?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，关于夏令时周末最后一小时睡眠与全国范围内事故和坠机事件之间的关系，我们了解些什么？

sentences.en: Well, there are several studies that examine this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几项研究对此进行了考察。

sentences.en: Some of my favorite studies examine car crashes.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一些研究是关于车祸的。

sentences.en: So the initial study published in 1996 found an elevated probability of car crashes following that spring daylight transition with a noticeable increase in both crashes and traffic fatalities.
sentences.zh: 1996年发表的初步研究发现，在春季夏令时转换后，车祸发生的概率升高，车祸和交通死亡人数都有显著增加。

sentences.en: There was a follow-up study in, I believe it was 2018, that basically replicated that pattern.
sentences.zh: 我相信在2018年有一项后续研究，基本复制了这一模式。

sentences.en: So we see a very clear spike in car crashes following that spring transition into daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到在春季转换为夏令时后，车祸数量有非常明显的激增。

sentences.en: One of my own papers looks at workplace injuries.
sentences.zh: 我自己的论文之一研究了工作场所的伤害。

sentences.en: And we deliberately studied mining injuries based on the idea that mining occurs underground.
sentences.zh: 我们特意研究了采矿伤害，基于采矿是在地下进行的这一事实。

sentences.en: So any changes in daylight pattern distribution would be parsed out of the study.
sentences.zh: 因此，日光模式分布的任何变化都会被排除在研究之外。

sentences.en: So we examined about a half a million mining injuries over a 25-year period.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了25年间大约50万起采矿伤害。

sentences.en: we found a spike on the Monday right after the change to daylight saving time of 5.6% in mining injuries and an even larger spike in injury severity as operationalized by number of lost work days due to the incident.
sentences.zh: 我们发现夏令时转换后的那个周一，采矿伤害激增了5.6%，而且伤害严重程度的激增幅度更大，这是通过事故导致的误工天数来衡量的。

sentences.en: Many of us don't get the recommended amount of sleep every night.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人每晚都没有获得建议的睡眠时间。

sentences.en: We know it can affect our well-being, our memory, our mood.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这会影响我们的健康、记忆力和情绪。

sentences.en: But what's more surprising is that a lack of sleep can cause poor decisions and even unethical behavior.
sentences.zh: 但更令人惊讶的是，睡眠不足会导致糟糕的决策，甚至是不道德的行为。

sentences.en: But of course, if the solution were really that simple, the problem would be solved by now.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果解决方案真的那么简单，问题早就解决了。

sentences.en: When we come back, getting to the root of our problems with sleep.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将深入探讨睡眠问题的根源。

sentences.en: Also, in our companion episode on Hidden Brain Plus, we take a deep dive into the effects of sleep deprivation on leaders, managers, and workplaces.
sentences.zh: 此外，在我们Hidden Brain Plus的配套剧集中，我们深入探讨了睡眠剥夺对领导者、管理者和工作场所的影响。

sentences.en: Turns out, sleep and sleep deprivation ought to be factors when you're deciding whether to work at a company or to invest in one.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，当你决定是否在一家公司工作或投资时，睡眠和睡眠剥夺应该成为考虑因素。

sentences.en: If you're a manager or a leader, you need to hear how sleep can affect your judgment and decision-making.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名管理者或领导者，你需要听听睡眠如何影响你的判断和决策。

sentences.en: If you're already a subscriber, that episode is available right now in this podcast feed.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经是订阅者，该剧集现在就在此播客源中提供。

sentences.en: It's titled, How Sleep Deprivation Affects Leaders.
sentences.zh: 标题是《睡眠剥夺如何影响领导者》。

sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅，请在support.hiddenbrain.org注册。

sentences.en: If you're using an Apple device, go to apple.co.hiddenbrain.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用苹果设备，请访问apple.co.hiddenbrain。

sentences.en: You'll instantly have access to all our subscriber-only content, and your support helps to sustain the reporting, writing, and fact-checking behind every episode of the show.
sentences.zh: 你将立即获得我们所有订阅者专享内容的访问权限，你的支持有助于维持节目每一集的报道、写作和事实核查。

sentences.en: Do you have questions or comments about sleep and how it affects your life?
sentences.zh: 你对睡眠及其如何影响你的生活有什么问题或评论吗？

sentences.en: Do you have a personal story about the effects of sleep deprivation that you would be willing to share with the Hidden Brain audience?
sentences.zh: 你是否有关于睡眠剥夺影响的个人故事愿意与Hidden Brain的听众分享？

sentences.en: If so, please find a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，请找一个非常安静的房间，用手机录制一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty.
Email the audio file to us using the address feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 将音频文件通过电子邮件发送给我们，地址是feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Again, that email address is feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，电子邮件地址是feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: We often think of sleep deprivation as a personal problem, something that affects how we feel, how productive we are, how well we can get through the day.
sentences.zh: 我们通常认为睡眠剥夺是一个个人问题，会影响我们的感受、工作效率以及我们度过一天的方式。

sentences.en: If we are tired or cranky from not getting enough rest, we assume the consequences will land on us.
sentences.zh: 如果我们因为休息不足而感到疲倦或暴躁，我们认为后果会由我们自己承担。

sentences.en: At the University of Washington, Chris Barnes studies the science of sleep and the effects of sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿大学，克里斯·巴恩斯研究睡眠科学和睡眠剥夺的影响。

sentences.en: He says the stakes are far higher than we imagine.
sentences.zh: 他说，风险远比我们想象的要高。

sentences.en: When people are chronically exhausted, that doesn't just affect their own health.
sentences.zh: 当人们长期精疲力竭时，这不仅影响他们自己的健康。

sentences.en: It can shape the safety of entire communities.
sentences.zh: 它还会影响整个社区的安全。

sentences.en: Chris, how much sleep do most people require and how much sleep do most people get?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，大多数人需要多少睡眠，而大多数人实际获得了多少睡眠？

sentences.en: So, most of us need between seven and nine hours.
sentences.zh: 大多数人需要7到9小时的睡眠。

sentences.en: Of course, people hear that and they hear, oh, okay, seven is fine.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们听到这个会觉得，哦，好吧，7小时没问题。

sentences.en: So, you might be one of the people who needs seven, but you might be one of the people who needs nine.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能是需要7小时的那类人，但也可能是需要9小时的那类人。

sentences.en: So, most of us are in that range, seven to nine.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们大多数人都在这个范围内，7到9小时。

sentences.en: For school-age children, ten or maybe even more for the youngest school-age children would be beSt.
sentences.zh: 对于学龄儿童，10小时甚至更多对年龄最小的学龄儿童来说是最好的。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, neither children nor adults are typically getting as much sleep as they should.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，儿童和成年人通常都没有获得他们应该获得的睡眠量。

sentences.en: Almost all of those people who are sleeping six hours need more than six hours.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有那些只睡6小时的人都需要超过6小时的睡眠。

sentences.en: Most of them probably need seven to nine like everyone else.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人可能像其他人一样需要7到9小时。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, a large number of people believe they are short-sleep superheroes
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，很多人认为自己是“短睡眠超人”，

sentences.en: and that maybe it's fine for everyone else to get eight hours of sleep,
sentences.zh: 认为也许其他人睡8小时没问题，

sentences.en: but I'll be just totally fine if I get four hours of sleep because I'm somehow above the need for sleep.
sentences.zh: 但我如果只睡4小时也会完全没问题，因为我不知何故不需要那么多睡眠。
这是一种不幸的普遍信念。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the importance of not just enough sleep, but of getting deep sleep?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈不仅要保证睡眠充足，还要保证深度睡眠的重要性吗？

sentences.en: So, when I talk about sleep, I usually talk about both sleep duration as well as sleep quality.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我谈论睡眠时，我通常会谈论睡眠时长和睡眠质量。

sentences.en: And sleep quality is a little bit harder to understand, but the central aspect there is getting into really deep sleep.
sentences.zh: 睡眠质量有点难理解，但核心方面是进入深度睡眠。

sentences.en: The simplest way to think about deep sleep is if it's kind of difficult to wake you out of that sleep,
sentences.zh: 考虑深度睡眠最简单的方法是，如果很难把你从睡眠中唤醒，

sentences.en: that's a good indication, at least on the surface level, that you're getting to that deep sleep.
sentences.zh: 这至少在表面上是一个很好的迹象，表明你进入了深度睡眠。

sentences.en: So, we can really divide our states into three states.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以真正把我们的状态分为三种。

sentences.en: So, there's waking, there is REM sleep, rapid eye movement sleep, and there's non-rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 即清醒状态、快速眼动睡眠（REM睡眠）和非快速眼动睡眠。

sentences.en: And when we get to this deep N3 non-rapid eye movement sleep,
sentences.zh: 当我们进入这种深度的N3非快速眼动睡眠时，

sentences.en: there are some very important recovery processes that happen more so during that aspect of sleep
sentences.zh: 会有一些非常重要的恢复过程发生，这些过程在睡眠的这一阶段比在REM睡眠或清醒活动中发生得更多。

sentences.en: than during REM sleep or waking activity.
I do say that both REM sleep and deep non-REM sleep are both quite important,
sentences.zh: 我确实认为REM睡眠和深度非REM睡眠都很重要，

sentences.en: but that deep non-REM sleep can be kind of hard to get sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但深度非REM睡眠有时可能比较难获得。

sentences.en: Let's talk about some interventions that can help us improve our sleep.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈一些可以帮助我们改善睡眠的干预措施。

sentences.en: Perhaps we should start by talking about the relationship that many of us have with our phones.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该从谈论我们许多人与手机的关系开始。

sentences.en: Yes, our phones are amazing devices that have lots of beneficial effects
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的手机是神奇的设备，有很多有益的影响，

sentences.en: and increasingly clearly some harmful effects as well.
sentences.zh: 但也越来越明显地产生了一些有害影响。

sentences.en: So, my colleagues and I conducted a study in which we examined smartphone use late at night.
sentences.zh: 所以，我和我的同事进行了一项研究，考察了深夜使用智能手机的情况。

sentences.en: We find that using these devices late at night tends to come at the cost of sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们发现深夜使用这些设备往往是以牺牲睡眠为代价的。

sentences.en: And as a result, people go to work the next day tired and they're not their best selves
sentences.zh: 结果，人们第二天带着疲惫去工作，无法发挥出最佳状态，

sentences.en: and they tend to be less engaged at work the next day.
sentences.zh: 而且第二天在工作中往往参与度较低。

sentences.en: So, there is sort of an ironic effect here where you might be trying to squeeze in a little bit more work
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一种讽刺的效果，你可能试图在深夜用手机多挤出一点工作时间，

sentences.en: late at night on your phone, but then you work less the next day as a result.
sentences.zh: 但结果第二天你的工作效率反而降低了。

sentences.en: So, there's not really a net gain there, but there is a net loss to your sleep and, of course,
sentences.zh: 所以，并没有真正的净收益，但你的睡眠确实有净损失，当然，

sentences.en: all the bad things that happen when you get less sleep.
sentences.zh: 还有睡眠不足带来的所有坏处。

sentences.en: So, you and others have also done research on the use of blue light filters.
sentences.zh: 所以，你和其他人也对蓝光过滤器的使用进行了研究。
谈谈这项工作吧，克里斯。

sentences.en: Does it help us when it comes to using our phones late at night?
sentences.zh: 它对我们深夜使用手机有帮助吗？

sentences.en: The ideal solution here is not to use our phones late at night,
sentences.zh: 这里理想的解决方案是不要在深夜使用手机，

sentences.en: but it is good to have some other tools that can help to mitigate some of these effects.
sentences.zh: 但拥有一些其他工具来帮助减轻其中一些影响也是好的。

sentences.en: Blue light, unfortunately, suppresses the production of melatonin,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，蓝光会抑制褪黑素的产生，
